comment: The features ui-look.js shows, one entry each: what it is, and the settings, commands and views of package.json that belong to it. Every step of ui-look.js names the features it shows. A feature that cannot be shown in a window says why in notShown and needs no step. A feature that works through Agent Plus also names, under agentPlus, the settings, commands and views of Agent Plus's package.json it uses; agentPlusOther lists the rest of Agent Plus's, with why they are not this extension's. window names the steps of ui.js, the window test CI runs, that assert a feature in code; relay names the options of the steward's script (claude-plugin/agent-work-plan/hooks/steward-relay.py, send being the message with no option) that belong to a feature. stewardActions lists the features that describe what a steward does or what it is told. test/check.js checks that every setting, command and view is listed here exactly once, those of Agent Plus against the Agent Plus it can find, that every other feature has a step, that every option of the steward's script belongs to exactly one feature, that every steward action has a ui-look.js step and a ui.js step, and that every window step named exists in ui.js.

features.what: A time on each of your messages and on every block of a reply, start->end on a tool call; Claude Code's own message times are hidden while these show.
On the first row of each reply: how long the turn took, the share of the context window in use, the cost so far, the model and its effort.
Turning off and on the times, the reply figures and the sub-agent tags at once, without a reload.
Your own messages: a bar down their left edge, and a text color when one is set.
Rows that came from a sub-agent carry a tag with its task.
features.notShown: the fake model starts its helper only in the background, and the Claude Code build this test installs draws none of a background helper's own messages in the conversation, so no row carries a tag

features.what: A footer control that shows all rows, only the main thread, or only one sub-agent.
The rail on the panel's right edge (to the top, previous, the list, next, to the bottom) and the list of your messages behind it, with times, a filter box and a highlighted row on hover.

A footer button that turns Claude Code's Focus view on and off; Focus view hides thinking and tool calls. Once you open tool calls by hand, the button shows the unfolded arrows, and a press folds them again without turning Focus view off.
While Focus view is on and a turn runs, the working line says which tool ran last or is running, and for how long.
This extension's footer buttons beside Claude Code's own, and the hover label of each.
The round usage meter stays in the footer; resting on it shows a breakdown with what the work plan added.
The footer button that mutes the end-of-turn sounds, and its two states.
The footer's info button and its box: session id, process id, starting folder, transcript and its size, token mode.

An image a reply gives by path is drawn at most 640 by 480 px; a click shows a scaled-down one large and a click or Escape closes it; an image at a web address stays a link; switched off, an image shows as its text and path.

Another conversation named in a reply by its title, by its title in corner brackets or by the first 8 characters of its session id is drawn as a link like Claude Code's own; hovering names the conversation and its agent, and a click opens it in the window that shows it.
window: conversation links: ids, code, own and placeholder titles, late and another agent

features.what: A line as wide as the message box, right above it, saying where the conversation's work plan stands: a track of the open rows by state, their count, the row being worked on with its state's mark, a count of the questions waiting for you in the status bar's warning yellow, and an arrow; hovering shows that row's whole title and lists the open rows; a click opens Agent Plus's work plan view at the conversation, and a click on the question count opens its Answer view at the question; the bar is compact in a narrow panel, and a conversation with no plan has none.

The footer's button that counts background work, its dot green while any of that work runs, and the map it opens: first the conversation's own row, under its own heading and with the same dot as its tab; then a section for each kind of work - Claude Code's subagents and background tasks, commands left running detached, scheduled prompts, claude -p workers and claude --bg sessions - each under a heading in capitals with its count and a line above it, and each row this extension adds is a card like Claude Code's: a dot, a title line and a line under it.

The claude --bg sessions a conversation started: its Agents button counts them, with a green dot while one runs; its agent map lists them, each state in its own colour, and keeps a finished one with its result.
A message from another conversation that got only a quiet reply (a dash) leaves nothing on screen: no dot, no fold row, no blank line.
A warning the page shows when its lookups stop finding the panel's messages; a working panel shows none.
A filled green dot on a Claude Code tab's logo, at its top right, and on its logo in Agent Plus's session list, while a turn runs.
A green ring, hollow in the middle, on a Claude Code tab's logo and on its logo in Agent Plus's session list, once the turn has ended and only background work still runs.

While Claude Code waits for you to answer a permission prompt or a choice: a filled red dot on a Claude Code tab's logo, and on its logo in Agent Plus's session list the filled blue dot Agent Plus uses for a dialog.
Once the conversation has stopped and nothing runs: no dot on a Claude Code tab's logo, blue or any other, and none on its row in Agent Plus's session list.

A white envelope (U+2709) at the end of a Claude Code tab's title, after a steward's crown, and an envelope icon after its title in Agent Plus's session list, while the conversation has a reply not read yet; it goes once the conversation is shown.
Claude Code's own session list, its icon in the Activity Bar, is hidden while the setting is on, and shown again when it is turned off.
Sessions started with claude --bg or claude -p are left out of the session list.

Claude Code's conversations in Agent Plus's session list, beside the other agents', each with its title and the Claude Code logo. The one open here has a solid stripe, background runs are left out, and a click opens a conversation in a tab.

A Claude Code conversation that a terminal has open, as Claude Code's record of the process says: its row in Agent Plus's session list is dimmed with an outlined stripe, and its hover says which terminal session and process.
A note above Agent Plus's session list, with the Claude Code logo, asks whether to hide Claude Code's own session list and offers Hide It and Keep It; it goes once answered.

The Claude Code part of Account & usage at the top of Agent Plus's session list: how Claude Code signs in unless with a claude.ai account, and the conversation in front with its estimated cost, time in API calls, time since it started and lines changed, or a line saying it has no figures yet or that no conversation runs in the window.
window: the figures of a conversation in Agent Plus's list

features.what: Resting on a Claude Code row in Agent Plus's session list opens a box under it: Claude Code and the row's section, the session id, when it started and was last active, and where it is open: in a tab of this window, in another VS Code window, or in a terminal.
The Steward panel at the bottom of the window: the conversations open in windows, with ticks.
A steward's tab shows one crown after its title, and its row in Agent Plus's session list a crown icon after it.

A conversation can have several stewards, and a steward has none: in a steward's panel only another steward's box is greyed, with a hover label saying why; a row that other stewards also manage ends in a light eye with their number; hovering over it lists them, and each name links to that steward's conversation.

New conversations, a switch beside "All, including new ones" in the Steward panel: the steward manages every conversation that starts after it is turned on, except stewards, and conversations already open keep their ticks.

Renaming a steward through Claude Code's own rename: the box holds no mark, whatever is typed the name is stored without crown, envelope or bell, and the tab and the list still show exactly one crown, first.
Renaming a conversation with a reply not read yet through its session list row's rename box: envelopes and crowns typed into the name are not stored, and it still shows exactly one envelope, last.
A steward passes a message on: Claude Code Plus types it into the managed conversation in the window that shows it, which sends it as your own message.
A steward's message is held back when another steward sent a message to the same conversation in the last 30 minutes: the script prints that message and who sent it, and --anyway sends it after all.
A steward renames a conversation it manages, and Claude Code records the new title.
A steward closes a managed conversation's editor tab, deleting nothing; one that is working, waiting for an answer or running background work only once the user has confirmed.
A steward starts a new conversation in the window that has a folder open, sends it the first message and then manages it; it can list the open windows and their folders.

A steward opens a conversation that no window shows, in an editor tab of the window whose first folder is where Claude Code keeps the conversation, passes it a message and has it ticked; not while a window shows it or another process runs it.
window: a steward reopening a conversation in the window of its folder

features.what: A managed conversation can hand one of its stewards a message that belongs elsewhere, and the steward gets it as a notice from Claude Code Plus. It goes to the one --to names, else the one whose message started its turn, else the one you typed to last. On native Windows the answer says the steward cannot be reached.

A steward changes its own list or switches when you ask for it in the steward conversation; when the request comes from a notice, a handoff or another conversation's message, it changes nothing and says why.
Claude Code Plus sends a steward a notice when a conversation it manages starts waiting for the user; not on native Windows.
A steward's link to a conversation, in a reply or on a Steward panel row, brings that conversation's tab to the front in whichever window shows it; a link to one open nowhere says so.
A title too long for its row ends in an ellipsis in the session list and the Steward panel, and the envelope stays in view after it, at the row's end.
In a light theme the envelope on the tab title is drawn in its one-colour text form, readable on the light background, and the envelope icon in Agent Plus's session list in the text colour.
Agent Plus's work plan view in the side bar, showing the conversation's plan, read from the plan files this extension's plugin keeps.

The pen at the end of a row in Agent Plus's work plan view brings the plan's conversation to the front, first opening it in a tab here if it is not open in one. Its message box then holds "About row N (title): " after anything already typed there, with the focus in the box and nothing sent. When that cannot be done, Agent Plus puts the text on the clipboard and says why.
window: writing about a work plan row

features.what: Agent Plus's Conversations view at the bottom of the window, listing Claude Code conversations and their questions, and the Answer view for one question.
An answer sent from Agent Plus's Answer view arrives in the conversation as your own message.

Agent Plus's notice, with Open and Dismiss, when a Claude Code conversation starts to wait for you or stops with an unread reply while the window with the focus does not show it, and the status bar's count of the conversations waiting for you, which includes those that window shows behind other editors and leaves out unread replies; there is no notice for the conversation in front.

Agent Plus's notice says what a conversation waits for: the tool it asks to run, a question, a plan to review; Claude Code's own notice of the same wait is left out meanwhile; what starts to wait while no window has the focus is shown once when a window has it again, one notice for each conversation.
window: notices of what a conversation waits for

features.what: Agent Plus: Show Status names this extension's Claude Code source and the folder of its plans.
Agent Plus's token mode entry in the status bar; the info box names the mode.
Claude Code Plus: Settings opens VS Code's settings at this extension's own.
Claude Code Plus: Show Status says whether Claude Code's two files are patched, and the token mode.
Claude Code Plus: Show How Long Opening a Panel Took shows the recorded panel-opening times.
Installing the work plan plugin again, and the confirmation before it stops being loaded.
This extension's additions in a narrow editor and a narrow side bar.
Everything this extension draws, in a light theme.
A short sound when a turn finishes, permission is asked or Claude asks a question.
features.notShown: a sound; the mute button that controls it is shown under chime-mute

features.what: Hooks that put the plan's open rows in front of Claude every turn, and the offer of a plan to a long conversation without one.
features.notShown: text added to Claude's context; nothing is drawn

features.what: Each conversation is asked to keep a brief of itself, which Agent Plus shows on a click.
features.notShown: the request is text in Claude's context, and the brief exists only once a live model has written one

features.what: Claude is told the time zone the panel is read in.
The conversation is told when a command it left running detached stops, and when a background session ends.
How long a pin keeps a conversation from Claude Code's transcript cleanup while no window is open.
features.notShown: changes file times on disk; the pin on screen looks the same

features.what: Claude Code tabs that VS Code did not restore after a lost remote connection are opened again.
features.notShown: needs a window that lost its remote connection; this window is local

features.what: Background Claude Code tabs load when the window starts, not when first clicked.
features.notShown: happens during start-up, each tab in front for a moment; afterwards the window looks the same either way

features.what: A conversation that runs in two Claude Code processes at once. Its Steward panel row gives the number of processes and has a Stop the old process button; its row in Agent Plus's session list shows the same number after the title, with "Open in N processes at once" in the hover.
window: a conversation run by two processes

features.what: Claude Code Plus: Remove from Claude Code restores Claude Code's original files.
features.notShown: it needs a reload, after which the remaining steps would run without the patch, and it rewrites the shared cache's copy of Claude Code; the window test, whose copy is its own, removes it last

agentPlusOther.why: VS Code's own limit on requests in flight for webview tabs, which Agent Plus edits in VS Code's files; nothing of this extension's
